title: Chapter 24 — The Symmetry Filter with Density Matrices: Exact under Uniform T1 Relaxation (Even Mid-Circuit), T1 Ratios, Failure under Dephasing and ZNE Rescue
text:
24.1 Why the filter is exact under uniform T1, also between gates
Updated: November 15, 2026
In the weight-1 sector, the no-jump Kraus operator of amplitude damping, \(K_0^{\otimes n}\) with \(K_0=\mathrm{diag}(1,\sqrt{1-\gamma})\), multiplies every \(|e_k\rangle\) by the same \(\sqrt{1-\gamma}\) (a single excited qubit); the jump \(K_1\) sends the mass to \(|0\ldots0\rangle\) (weight 0), where the RBS act as the identity and from where it never returns. Therefore, after \(L\) gates with uniform \(T_1\) in each, \[\rho_S^{\text{filtered}}=\rho_S^{\text{ideal}}\ \ (\text{coherences included}),\qquad \text{rate}=(1-\gamma)^L .\] Verified: \(\|\rho_S-\rho_S^{\text{ideal}}\|_\infty=1.2\cdot10^{-16}\), rate \(0.7351=(0.95)^6\). Without the filter the reading drifts: \(-393\to-289\) m-qg (\(\gamma=0.05\)), \(\to-103\) m-qg (\(\gamma=0.2\)) (exact). It generalizes the result of Ch. 23 (histograms) to states with coherence. Uniform amplitude damping acts on the weight-1 sector as a global scalar plus an irreversible leak to weight 0, so sector postselection restores the exact state mid-circuit.

24.2 T1 ratios (F5): exact correction only for final noise
Non-uniform \(T_1\) \(\gamma_k\) applied at the end: \(p(e_k)=(1-\gamma_k)\,p^{\text{ideal}}(e_k)\) exactly ⇒ dividing by \((1-\gamma_k)\) (calibrated, Ch. 30) recovers \(y=-0.3933\). Applied between gates, the distortion does not commute with the RBS: filtered \(y=+0.0746\) (error \(0.468\)) and the final correction is not enough (mixed). Rule: \(T_1\) ratios only with gate times \(\ll T_1\) of the slowest qubits; measure \(\gamma_k\) per qubit (Ch. 30).

24.3 Dephasing: the filter does not protect; ZNE does (F6)
Dephasing conserves the weight but destroys coherences inside the sector, invisible to the filter. With \(p=0.02\) per gate: filtered error \(0.0551\); Richardson over \(\lambda\in\{1,2,3\}\) (\(y=-0.3382,-0.2939,-0.2584\)) extrapolates to \(-0.3914\) (error \(0.0019\), \(\times28.7\)) at the cost of \(3\times\) circuits (exact sim.; hardware unverified). Recommended combination: filter (removes \(T_1\) and leaks) + ZNE (residual dephasing); order of application: filter each \(\lambda\), then extrapolate.

text:
25.1 Assignment error is an affine map in m-qg
Updated: November 15, 2026
With \(e_{01}=P(\text{read }1|0)\), \(e_{10}=P(\text{read }0|1)\): \[m'=(1-e_{01}-e_{10})\,m+1000\,(e_{10}-e_{01}),\qquad m^\star=\frac{1000\,(e_{10}-e_{01})}{e_{01}+e_{10}}\ \ (\text{fixed point, zero bias}).\] Instance \(e_{01}=0.02,e_{10}=0.06\): \(-1000\to-880\), \(0\to+40\), \(+1000\to+960\) m-qg; \(m^\star=+500\) m-qg. The “pull effect” is the contraction \(0.92\) plus the shift \(+40\) m-qg; the cost of an \(X\) gate measured in §168 (\(1.64\) linear m-qg) is this same map with \(e\sim10^{-3}\) (exact, tested on hardware §168). Assignment error is an affine contraction of the m-qg axis with a drag-free fixed point \(m^\star\).

text:
26.1 Fidelity kernel for product maps: closed form in qg
Updated: November 15, 2026
For \(|\psi(x)\rangle=\bigotimes_q|\alpha_q,\varphi_q\rangle\) (angles in qga) with Bloch vectors \(\mathbf r_q\): \[k(x,x')=|\langle\psi(x)|\psi(x')\rangle|^2=\prod_{q=1}^n\frac{1+\mathbf r_q\cdot\mathbf r'_q}{2}\quad(\text{exact, }10^{-13}).\] The readout kernel \(\prod_q(1+qg_Zqg_Z')/2\) (one basis) is not the fidelity: it omits \(qg_X,qg_Y\). Estimation costs: SWAP test (1 ancilla, \(n\) cSWAP), inversion test \(U(x')^\dagger U(x)\) (0 ancillas, depth \(2L\), read \(P(|0\ldots0\rangle)\)). The product-map fidelity kernel has a closed form in Bloch vectors; the \(Z\)-only kernel is a different, classical object.

text:
26.2 Exponential concentration: the kernel analogue of the barren plateau
Random product features (\(\alpha\sim U[0,500]\), \(\varphi\sim U[0,1000]\) qga): \(\mathbb E[k]\approx(1/4)^{n/2}\) and \(\mathrm{Var}[k]\) falls from \(5.5\cdot10^{-2}\) (\(n=2\)) to \(2.1\cdot10^{-5}\) (\(n=10\)); shots for \(\sigma_k=\mathbb E[k]/10\): \(3\cdot10^2\to10^5\). The kernel is dimensionless: the qga unit does not intervene (consistent with Ch. 9 §4: against as a mitigation). It is the same phenomenon as the plateau: useful information is diluted in \(2^n\) dimensions.

text:
26.3 Unary sector kernel: (x· x’)², polynomial, no concentration
With the unary loader of Ch. 23, \(|x\rangle=\sum_kx_k|e_k\rangle\) ⇒ \(k_u(x,x')=(x\cdot x')^2\) — polynomial of degree 2, estimable by ancilla-free inversion test (\(2(n-1)\) RBS) with \(P(|e_0\rangle)\), exact to \(10^{-12}\). For random unit vectors: \(\mathbb E[k_u]=1/n\) and \(\mathrm{Var}[k_u]\sim2/n^2\) (\(n=4:6.2\cdot10^{-2}\); \(n=16:6.5\cdot10^{-3}\)): polynomial decay. Shots at \(\sigma=\mathbb E/10\) with \(n=6\): \(507\) versus \(6.4\cdot10^3\) for the product map. In addition, the weight-1 sector enables the symmetry filter: exact \(T_1\) (Ch. 24) and readout at \(O(e_{01}e_{10})\) (Ch. 25). Honest limit: \(k_u\) is a classical (polynomial) kernel — the advantage is in noise and budget engineering, not expressivity (exact; learning advantage no gain).

text:
27.1 XY conserves the weight: the quantum walk is a sequence of RBS
Updated: November 15, 2026
\(H_{XY}=J\sum_k(X_kX_{k+1}+Y_kY_{k+1})/2\) commutes with the Hamming weight; in the weight-1 sector it is the adjacency matrix \(J A_n\) (continuous-time quantum walk of one exciton). The propagator of one link is exactly an RBS (Givens) gate of angle \(Jt\) — the same gate as the unary loader (Ch. 23) — so the even-odd Trotter step is an RBS network with \(\Sigma p=1\) exact, and the symmetry filter of Ch. 24 applies unchanged to the dynamics. First-order Trotter error (\(n=6\), \(J=1\), \(t=2\)): \(0.317\) (1 step, RBS of \(318\) qga), \(0.111\) (4), \(0.029\) (16), \(0.0073\) (64 steps, RBS of \(5.0\) qga) ∝ \(dt\) (exact). Per-site reading \(qg_Z^{(k)}=1-2p_k\): \([998,735,168,366,787,947]\) m-qg at \(t=2\). XY dynamics in the weight-1 sector is a Givens/RBS network: weight conservation is exact, the symmetry filter transfers verbatim, and first-order Trotter error scales as \(dt\).

27.2 Affine Bloch channels: a single calibration (M,c)
Every 1-qubit channel is \(\mathbf r\mapsto M\mathbf r+\mathbf c\) (12 numbers). \(T_1\): \(M=\mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{1-\gamma},\sqrt{1-\gamma},1-\gamma)\), \(\mathbf c=(0,0,\gamma)\) (matches Kraus to \(10^{-14}\)); dephasing: \(M=\mathrm{diag}(1-2p,1-2p,1)\); readout (Ch. 25): \(M_{zz}=1-e_{01}-e_{10}\), \(c_z=e_{10}-e_{01}\). Composition is another pair \((M,\mathbf c)\): \(T_1(0.2)\circ\text{dephasing}(0.05)\circ\text{readout}(0.02,0.06)\) takes \((0.6,0,0.5)\to(0.483,0,0.592)\), \(+500\to+592\) m-qg, \(qg_\tau\) \(0.624\to0.645\). Rule: calibrate the whole chain as a single affine map (12 parameters) instead of three models, and use \(qg_\tau\) (Ch. 5) as the purity invariant (exact).

27.3 One-qubit varQTE: McLachlan with RY(θ) in qga
\(H=\omega Z/2\) from \(|+\rangle\): \(qg_Z(\tau)=-\tanh(\omega\tau)\) (exact). With the ansatz \(R_Y(\theta)|0\rangle\), the McLachlan equation is \(\dot\theta=\omega\sin\theta\) (metric \(g=1/4\) in rad, \((2\pi/1000)^2/4\) in qga); explicit Euler converges as \(1/\text{steps}\): error \(9.2\cdot10^{-3}\) (30), \(9.2\cdot10^{-5}\) (3000), final \(-995\) m-qg. It is the thermal state of Ch. 11 (\(qg_Z=\tanh\)) as a fixed point: 1 parameter, 0 ancillas, no plateaus (\(P=1\)). For \(P>1\) apply Ch. 9 (regularized \(F_Z\) metric), never plain descent in \(qg_Z\) (THEORY_CORE §2.1).

title: Chapter 28 — Chemistry and Optimization in the Weight Sector: the Electron-Count Witness in m-qg, Number Checks, RBS-Based PCA and “Exactly-K” QAOA
text:
28.1 Counting electrons with the register readout
Updated: November 16, 2026
In Jordan–Wigner, qubit \(q\) is a spin-orbital with occupation \((1-qg_{Z,q})/2\). For \(N\) electrons in \(n\) spin-orbitals the ideal mean reading is \(\overline{qg_Z}=1-2N/n\) (0 m-qg for \(N=2,n=4\)). The witness \(W=1000(\overline{qg_Z}-(1-2N/n))\) is 0 if the circuit conserved \(N\). Under \(T_1\) of rate \(\gamma\) on a register with mean occupation 1/2, \(W=+1000\gamma\) m-qg exactly: \(+20,+50,+100\) m-qg for \(\gamma=0.02,0.05,0.10\) (exact). The symmetry check is the familiar one from quantum chemistry; qang contributes the unit (m-qg) and the zero-cost witness. The electron count is a direct readout of the register: the witness is exactly \(1000\gamma\) m-qg under \(T_1\).

text:
29.1 Four-qubit amplitude-damping code with syndrome in m-qg
Updated: November 16, 2026
\(|0_L\rangle=(|0000\rangle+|1111\rangle)/\sqrt2\), \(|1_L\rangle=(|0011\rangle+|1100\rangle)/\sqrt2\) (Leung 1997, exact: not a qang invention). The syndrome is the weight parity: \(ZZZZ=(-1)^{w}\), that is, the \(qg_{ZZZZ}\) reading in m-qg: \(+1000\) for the code and \(1000(1-2P_{\text{odd}})\) after noise (\(819.0\) m-qg with \(\gamma=0.05\)). With even weight nothing is done; with odd weight an isometry per jumped qubit returns to the code (\(\sum R^\dagger R=I\) to \(10^{-12}\)). Result with \(T_1\) of rate \(\gamma\) per qubit, mean fidelity over the 6 Pauli eigenstates:
The log-log slope is 1.00 unencoded and 1.99 encoded: the code cancels the order-\(\gamma\) term. It is the same mechanism by which the sector filter is exact under \(T_1\) (Ch. 24): the jump changes the weight. Limits: (i) \(P_{\text{odd}}\approx2\gamma\); (ii) it only helps while \(\gamma<\gamma^*\approx0.177\); (iii) encoding without recovering is worse (\(1.98\cdot10^{-2}\) versus \(3.34\cdot10^{-3}\) with \(\gamma=0.01\)); (iv) the syndrome requires 1 ancilla and 4 CNOT, not included in the model, which contains only \(T_1\) (exact in simulation; hardware unverified). The 4-qubit AD code removes the \(O(\gamma)\) term (log-log slope 1.99 vs 1.00) and its syndrome is the \(qg_{ZZZZ}\) reading.

A circuit cut must carry at least \(\lceil\log_2\text{rank}\rceil\) wires (lower bound on the state). For weight \(w\) and cut \(m\,|\,n-m\) the generic rank is \(\sum_k\min\big(\binom mk,\binom{n-m}{w-k}\big)\) (verified with SVD for \(n=8\), \(m=4\)):

30.1 T1: where to measure
Updated: November 16, 2026
After waiting \(t\) from \(|1\rangle\), \(qg_Z(t)=1-2e^{-t/T_1}\) (m-qg \(=1000\,qg_Z\)). The log-linear fit recovers \(T_1\) to \(10^{-9}\) without noise. With binomial shots, the Fisher information per shot is \(x^2e^{-x}/(1-e^{-x})\) with \(x=t/T_1\), maximal at \(x^*=1.5936\), where \(qg_Z=+594\) m-qg. With 2000 shots per point and \(T_1=100\) (4 points):
The information at the optimal delay is \(\times3.6\) that of the short delay, with the same shots (exact; the maximum-likelihood estimator reaches the bound). The experimental decision: measure near \(1.6\,T_1\), not at short delays; but it requires knowing \(T_1\) in advance (two-stage plan). The Fisher information per shot peaks at \(t=1.59\,T_1\) (\(+594\) m-qg); short delays cost \(\times3.6\) in information.

30.2 Readout: e01, e10 and their budget
Preparing \(|0\rangle\) and \(|1\rangle\) gives \(e_{01},e_{10}\) with binomial error: with \((40/2000,\,120/2000)\) one gets \(e_{01}=0.0200\pm0.0031\) and \(e_{10}=0.0600\pm0.0053\). For \(\sigma_e=0.002\) with \(e=0.02\) one needs \(e(1-e)/\sigma^2=4900\) shots (exact). The affine readout of Ch. 25 is inverted exactly: \(+600\to+592.0\) m-qg measured \(\to+600.0\) corrected. Limit (Ch. 25, criterion §108): the correction only holds if \(1-e_{01}-e_{10}\) is stable between calibration and use.

text:
30.3 XEB / HOP and fidelity
With global depolarizing noise, \(\mathrm{HOP}=f\cdot\mathrm{HOP}_{PT}+(1-f)/2\), \(\mathrm{HOP}_{PT}=(1+\ln2)/2=0.8466\). For \(n=8\) Haar states (300 samples): \(f=1.0\to0.8460\), \(0.7\to0.7422\) (predicted \(0.7426\)), \(0.3\to0.6038\); the recovered fidelity is \(0.998,\,0.699,\,0.299\) (exact, simulation). The threshold \(\mathrm{HOP}>2/3\) is equivalent to \(f\ge0.481\). Limit: HOP is a global output quantity; it does not distinguish between depolarizing and coherent noise, and measures \(f\) only under the depolarizing model.

text:
30.4 Static ZZ in qga
With \(H=\zeta ZZ/4\) qubit 0 rotates \(\pm\zeta t/2\) depending on the neighbor: the relative phase is \(\zeta t\) rad \(=1000\,\zeta t/(2\pi)\) qga. For \(\zeta/2\pi=0.2\) MHz and \(t=1.3\) µs that is 260.0 qga. In a Ramsey readout, \(qg_X=+684.5\) m-qg in both cases (the cosine is even) and \(qg_Y=\pm729.0\) m-qg: the shift shows in the \(Y\) basis, not in \(X\) (exact).

section: 30.5 Control quantization: changing unit does not help
text:
30.5 Control quantization: changing unit does not help
Rounding to \(L=2^b\) levels per turn leaves \(\sigma=1/(L\sqrt{12})\) turns: 4.517 qga at 6 bits, 1.125 qga at 8, 0.282 qga at 10; in radians they are the same numbers scaled by \(2\pi/1000\) (to \(10^{-12}\)). It is a property of the grid, not of the unit: no gain from choosing qga over radians (no gain); a dyadic DAC moreover does not represent the decimal grid of 1000 qga except for \(b\le3\).

title: Chapter 31 — Methodology: Pre-Registered Falsification with SHA-256, Exact p-values, Holm Correction and Shot Budget
text:
31.1 Register before measuring
Updated: November 16, 2026
A prediction is a closed dictionary (claim, metric, threshold, direction, \(\alpha\), seed, date, script). It is serialized as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, UTF-8) and its SHA-256 is stored in a commit prior to the measurement. Verified with prediction F-31-01 (“the \(N\) mod 4 filter returns the ideal energy under uniform \(T_1\)”, Ch. 28): the hash (ec1f27a5b1d16582…) does not depend on key order and any change in the 9 fields invalidates it (9/9). This is the part that prevents moving the threshold afterwards (exact). Limit: the hash proves that the text did not change, not that the commit predates the data; that is given by the date of the remote commit. The registration is a SHA-256 of a canonical JSON; it detects any later change to the claim, threshold or seed.

text:
31.2 Deciding with an exact test
For “\(p>p_0\)” with \(k\) successes in \(n\) shots: confirmed if \(P(X\ge k)\le\alpha\); refuted if \(P(X\le k)\le\alpha\); otherwise inconclusive (not interpreted as support). With \(p_0=0.5\): \(P(X\ge60\mid n=100)=0.02844\) (confirmed), \(P(X\ge530\mid n=1000)=0.03101\) (confirmed), \(k=40\) (refuted), \(k=55\) (inconclusive). The tails match scipy.stats.binom to \(10^{-12}\) (exact).

title: Chapter 31 — Methodology: Pre-Registered Falsification with SHA-256, Exact p-values, Holm Correction and Shot Budget
text:
31.3 Several predictions: Holm
With 20 null hypotheses and 3000 repetitions (\(n=400\)): without correction, \(P(\ge1\ \text{false positive})=0.656\); with Holm–Bonferroni, 0.042 (\(\le0.05\)). This is why the protocol registers the complete family of predictions, not only those that turned out well (exact, simulation).

text:
31.4 Shot budget
Detecting \(p=0.6\) against \(p_0=0.5\) (\(\alpha=0.05\)): \(n=224\) for power \(0.90\) (achieved \(0.911\)), \(n=405\) for \(0.99\). Detecting \(0.52\): \(n=5435\) (\(\times24.3\approx(0.10/0.02)^2\)): the cost grows as \(1/\Delta^2\). A prediction that cannot reach power with the available budget must be registered as untestable, not as pending luck (exact).

“Confirmed” here means exact in analysis or in simulation, not measured on a device. No sub-measure of Ch. 7–31 has tested on hardware as its primary status. The only row that cites hardware as a caveat is readout_drag_affine (Ch. 25, §168 of the notes). Of the 82 exact rows, 18 carry a caveat (mostly hardware unverified): the result is correct, but its transfer to a device was not verified. The remaining 64 have no caveat, and several of them are identities (for example, \(F\preceq4g\) with \(P=8\), or exact \(N\) mod 4 for \(N=2,n=4\)).
Zero measured gain means that no chapter of this rewrite measures a gain against a classical or standard method on real data; the “without qang vs with qang” comparisons are of resources, of analytic exactness or of simulations.

title: Chapter 33 — String Theory: What qang Measures Can and Cannot Say (the XX Chain as a c = 1 Free Boson)
text:
33.1 Scope: the only thing claimed
Updated: November 16, 2026
A bosonic string has a worldsheet described by a 1+1-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT); a compact free boson is the basic building block, with central charge \(c=1\). An XX spin chain (or free fermions on a lattice) is a lattice realization of that free boson. That is all this chapter takes from string theory: a lattice model whose continuum limit is a CFT with \(c=1\). No strings, gravity, extra dimensions, spectrum, T-duality or AdS/CFT are simulated: those claims remain not adopted (§33.7). The bosonic string requires matter with \(c=26\) to cancel the anomaly; the \(c=1\) chain neither satisfies it nor pretends to.

title: Chapter 33 — String Theory: What qang Measures Can and Cannot Say (the XX Chain as a c = 1 Free Boson)
text:
33.2 Model
Open chain of \(n\) sites, \(H=-\sum_i(c_i^\dagger c_{i+1}+\text{h.c.})\) with \(N=n/2\) fermions (≡ XX chain via Jordan–Wigner). The ground state is a Slater determinant and everything follows from \(C_{ij}=\langle c_i^\dagger c_j\rangle\). qang readings: \(qg_{Z,i}=1-2C_{ii}\) (m-qg \(=1000\,qg_Z\)) and connected \(qg_{ZZ}=\langle Z_iZ_j\rangle-\langle Z_i\rangle\langle Z_j\rangle=-4C_{ij}^2\) (Wick).

title: Chapter 33 — String Theory: What qang Measures Can and Cannot Say (the XX Chain as a c = 1 Free Boson)
section: 33.5 What qang does see: the power law
text:
33.5 What qang does see: the power law
The connected \(qg_{ZZ}\) of two sites at odd distance \(r\) is \(-4/(\pi r)^2\) in the infinite chain (scaling dimension 1). In open chains the log-log slope of \(\lvert qg_{ZZ}^c\rvert\) versus \(r\in\{3,\dots,31\}\) is \(-1.907\) (\(n=400\)), \(-1.952\) (\(800\)), \(-1.976\) (\(1600\)), toward \(-2\); at the center with \(r=5\): \(-16.37\) m-qg versus \(-4000/(5\pi)^2=-16.21\) m-qg (exact; the residual is an edge effect and decreases with \(n\)). It is a two-point reading: it costs \(O(n^2)\) pairs and gives only \(\lvert C_{ij}\rvert\), not the phase.

title: Chapter 33 — String Theory: What qang Measures Can and Cannot Say (the XX Chain as a c = 1 Free Boson)
section: 33.6 What qang does not see: local readings
text:
33.6 What qang does not see: local readings
At the center of the chain with \(n=128\): \(\lvert qg_Z\rvert\le1.8\cdot10^{-12}\) m-qg and \(qg_S=1.00000\) bits at all sites (particle-hole symmetry fixes \(C_{ii}=1/2\)). The block entropy, by contrast, grows from 0.773 (\(\ell=2\)) to 1.575 bits (\(\ell=64\)). A local reading is identical for \(\ell=2\) and \(\ell=64\): neither \(qg_Z\) nor \(qg_S\) can give \(c\) (against, consistent with Ch. 5, 7 and 18: \(qg_S\) is not an entanglement measure).

title: Chapter 33 — String Theory: What qang Measures Can and Cannot Say (the XX Chain as a c = 1 Free Boson)
section: 33.7 What this chapter does not say
text:
33.7 What this chapter does not say

It does not test string theory: reproducing \(c=1\) and an exponent \(-2\) in a spin chain is a property of the free-boson CFT, which also appears in a Heisenberg chain, in a Luttinger liquid and in many models unrelated to strings.
There is no evidence that the qg or qga unit simplifies anything in string theory: no quantity of the theory was found that is better expressed in m-qg (not adopted).
AdS/CFT, T-duality, string spectrum, compactification, strings with \(c=26\): unverified/not adopted; there is no code or verifier.
The relation to chapters 17–18 (black holes as scramblers) is one of quantum-information language, not a holographic verification.

34.6 Error inside the sector
The filter discards shots outside the sector; an error that conserves the weight passes entirely. With ideal RBS of \(\pi/2\) versus RBS\((\pi/2+0.3)\) (in_sector_error):

filter retention: 1.0 in both cases;
\(qg_Z\) of qubit 0: \(+1000.0\to+825.3\) m-qg: deviation of \(-174.7\) m-qg, invisible to the filter.

It is the same mechanism as in LiH (notes §50: the error is in the X/Y groups, out of reach of the Z filter). Those numbers are cited: LiH, 60 gates: 76.6 mHa raw versus 85.0 mHa with filter (unverified in this chapter).

section: 34.7 The weight-1 network is a classical quadratic form
text:
34.7 The weight-1 network is a classical quadratic form
In the single-excitation sector, the RBS network acts as an orthogonal matrix \(O\) on the loaded data \(v\), and
\[qg_Z^{(i)}=1-2\,(Ov)_i^2 .\]
weight1_qgz evaluates it in \(O(n^2)\); simulate_qgz_weight1 simulates the full circuit (\(2^n\) amplitudes). With \(n=5\) and 20 random networks the maximum deviation is \(4.4\cdot10^{-16}\). What the filter protects exactly from \(T_1\) is, for that same reason, simulable. No quantum advantage is claimed.

import numpy as np
from qang.qlimits import (ring_graph_state, plus_state, z_distribution, stabilizer_expectation, t1_noise_scan, is_monotone,

    assert np.max(np.abs(z_distribution(g) - z_distribution(p))) == 0.0
    assert np.allclose([stabilizer_expectation(g, i, 6) for i in range(6)], 1.0)
def test_t1_mean_qgz_monotone_and_qgs_not():

34.13 A single readout basis: no-go, \(C_Z\) and purity
Every quantity computed only from the distribution \(P_Z\) shares the root of §34.2. Here the general case is closed, not just the graph. \(H_Z\) is in bits; \(H_Z/n\) is labeled separately and never enters \(C_Z=\sum_i H(X_i)-H_Z\).
Diagonal-twin theorem. For every \(p\), \(\sigma_p=\sum_x p(x)|x\rangle\langle x|\) is completely separable and has exactly that distribution. No rule that uses only \(p\) (with \(qg_Z\), \(qg_S\), \(H_Z\), \(C_Z\) or any learned summary) can certify entanglement, even with infinitely many shots (diagonal_twin). It costs less than it seems: it only takes a separable state that reproduces it.

A bias in \(z\) does not remove it: \(\lvert a\rangle\lvert b\rangle\) and \(\mathrm{CZ}\lvert a\rangle\lvert b\rangle\), with \(z=(0.5,0.6)\), have \(P_Z=(0.60,0.15,0.20,0.05)\) and \(H_Z=1.533206\) bits; \(P_i=1\) versus \(0.76\); PT min. \(-0.346410\).
Purity. With the diagonal \(p\), the exact range of \(\mathrm{Tr}\rho^2\) is \([\sum_x p(x)^2,\,1]\); the extremes are \(\sigma_p\) and \(\lvert\psi_p\rangle=\sum_x\sqrt{p(x)}\lvert x\rangle\) (purity_range_from_z). The collision probability \(\sum p^2\) is purity only if \(\rho\) is diagonal in Z. For \(p=(0.6,0.15,0.2,0.05)\): \([0.4250,1]\).
\(C_Z\) is not entanglement, in both directions (total_correlation_z):

False negative: \(C_Z=0\) on the entangled graph state (edge and path).
False positive: \(\lvert\mathrm{GHZ}_3\rangle\) and the mixture \(\tfrac12(\lvert000\rangle\langle000\rvert+\lvert111\rangle\langle111\rvert)\) have the same \(P_Z\) and \(C_Z=2\) bits (the maximum); the mixture is separable (\(P=1/2\)).
Three-body dependence with independent pairs: the uniform mixture over even-parity strings has pairwise mutual information \(0\), \(H_Z=2\) and \(C_Z=1\) bit.
The result depends on the readout basis: \((I\otimes H)\lvert G_2\rangle=\lvert\Phi^+\rangle\) goes from \(H_Z=2\) to \(1\) and from \(C_Z=0\) to \(1\), with entanglement and purity intact.

\(H_Z=C_{\mathrm{rel},Z}=H_Z-S(\rho)\) only if \(\rho\) is pure (relative_entropy_coherence_z): in \(G_2\), \(2=2\); in \(I_4/4\), \(0\) versus \(H_Z=2\). And \(qg_S=h_2((1+qg_Z)/2)\) determines \(|qg_Z|\) but not its sign: it is not a second independent reading.
What does certify: a two-setting witness (witness_path, witness_radius). For the 3-qubit path, \(W'_3=2I-XZI-ZXZ-IZX\) takes the value \(-1\) on \(G_3\) and \(+2\) on the product and on \(I/8\). It is estimated with XZX (gives \(K_1\) and \(K_3\)) and ZXZ (gives \(K_2\)). With 1000 shots per setting and \(\delta=0.05\) the conservative radius is \(m\eta=0.293556\) (\(m=3\)): \(-1+0.2936<0\) certifies genuine tripartite entanglement. A non-negative value concludes nothing. The witness works for the 3-qubit and the 2-qubit path; it is not generalized to every graph.
Noise: two exact counterexamples to monotonicity. (i) Final dephasing \(\rho_t=(1-t)\lvert G_3\rangle\langle G_3\rvert+t\,I/8\): \(P_Z\) stays fixed and \(\langle W'_3\rangle=-1+3t\) (\(-1,\,0,\,+2\) at \(t=0,\,\tfrac13,\,1\)). (ii) Product under amplitude damping \(\gamma=0,\tfrac12,1\): \(H_Z=0,2,0\) bits and \(P=1,\tfrac14,1\) with \(C_Z=0\) always; neither entropy nor purity measures the amount of noise.
Shots. A mean in \([-1,1]\) with \(\varepsilon=0.05\) and \(\delta=0.05\) needs \(N=2952\) (Hoeffding; hoeffding_shots). For the entropy there is no analogous rule: the assumption-free bound (sufficient_shots_entropy, sufficient, not necessary, loose) gives \(N=133\,966\) (\(H_Z\), \(n=2\)), \(253\,199\) (\(H_Z\), \(n=3\)), \(1\,346\,071\) (\(C_Z\), \(n=2\)) and \(3\,973\,513\) (\(C_Z\), \(n=3\)). In addition, the plug-in \(C_Z\) is positive with uniform independent \(p\): bias \(\tfrac{2^n-1-n}{2N\ln 2}\) (plugin_cz_bias_uniform). With \(n=3\), \(N=100\) (1000 repetitions, seed 34): \(\hat H_Z=2.9478\), \(\hat C_Z=0.0307\) (theory \(0.0289\)) versus the exact \(3\) and \(0\); at \(N=10\,000\), \(0.0003\). It is statistical bias, not physical correlation.

35.2 What is taken to the chip
The reading of a real qubit is that of Ch. 1: \(qg_Z=2p_0-1\). What surrounds it changes: compilation to native gates, its own readout errors and per-shot credits. qang contributes three things, all in post-processing: the weight filter (if the circuit conserves it), the witness (fraction kept) and the reading in m-qg. The readout correction is affine:
\[m' = (1-e_0-e_1)\,m + 1000\,(e_1-e_0),\qquad e_0=P(1\mid 0),\ e_1=P(0\mid 1).\]
predicted_raw_mqg applies it and correct_mqg inverts it.

M2 (dispersion of the equator copies between 0.55 and 1.45 of the binomial \(\sigma\)): failed, with \(0.500\). The 10 copies spread half as much as shot noise allows. It remains unexplained; none is proposed.

The slope per X gate, fitted through the origin with \(k-1\) gates, is 1.64 m-qg (\(\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}=0.81\)). M3 passes, but the prediction’s design makes it poorly informative beyond \(k=15\) (recorded that way in the run).

35.8 What this chapter does not claim

There is no replication: each run is one day, one chip, one qubit (or 3). The 5-qubit, two-day replication is prepared (examples/iqm_milliqang_replication_qg.py) and not run.
“The chip was better than its model” (raw error \(0.062\) versus \(0.126\) of the simulated Garnet model; factor \(1.59\) versus \(2.16\)) uses simulations that were not re-run here: unverified.
qang.iqm (readout correction and chain choice) was written after the runs and was not tested on the real chip; it requires iqm-client. The runs were made with the scripts of examples/ and qang.interop.
IQM’s compilation advantage (12 CZ versus 18 two-qubit gates on IBM) was an optimization-level effect (3 versus 1), not a chip effect: at the same level they give the same. That count requires Qiskit and was not re-run here (unverified).

text:
36.3 Extras and what CI installs
parse_pyproject reads pyproject.toml with no external dependencies, and check_extras checks the three project rules:

the core depends only on numpy;
iqm is isolated from all (because iqm-client pins its own Qiskit);
the jax extra is bounded to <0.9.

CI installs pip install -e ".[all]": 14 packages, among them Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, scikit-learn and SciPy, but not JAX or Torch. Therefore every test that imports a module of the JAX group must be protected with pytest.importorskip("jax"): an unguarded import fails at collection and pytest exits with code 2, not 1. unguarded_tests computes, for each test file, the packages it requires (its own, those of the qang.x it imports and those of the examples/ scripts it imports, transitively) and returns those that are neither installed nor guarded:

of 192 test files: 0 unprotected.

This result rules out one cause of the Tests failure in CI; it does not identify the real cause. That remains pending from the log of the “Run tests” step.

text:
36.6 Guidelines by hardware type

Superconducting (IBM, IQM): compile with weight-conserving gates (XX+YY, RBS) and check it with qang.qlimits.preserves_weight or the analysis of qang.ibm; compare two-qubit gates at the same optimization level (Ch. 35); correct the readout with the calibration or with the two poles.
Ions (IonQ, Braket): all-to-all connectivity; the bit order is resolved in qang.interop. The H₂ run on the real machine was rejected before a job was accepted and was not charged.
On any platform: rehearse for free, measure the cost with a small test, pre-register before the main job (Ch. 31), read the token from an environment variable and do not spend without an explicit flag.

37.3 Landauer: one channel, one reading
\(G/G_0=\sum_nT_n=N/2+\tfrac12\sum_n qg_n\), with the saddle-point model \(T_n=1/(1+e^{-2\pi(V-n-1/2)/w})\) (\(w=0.45\)): identity to \(4.4\cdot10^{-16}\) (conductance_from_qg). The plateaus are at \(V=2,3,4\) with \(G/G_0=1,2,3\); each step is a channel crossing the equator. Conductance alone gives \(\sum T_n\); with shot noise \(S=\sum T_n(1-T_n)\) two simultaneously open channels are recovered (recover_two_channels): from \(G=1.3747\), \(S=0.2682\) come exactly \(T=0.9716\) and \(0.4031\). It is the usual technique; in qg, conductance reads the mean \(qg\) and noise the mean \(qg^2\).

37.6 Spin qubits in quantum dots
Charge-sensor readout has errors \(e_0=P(1\mid0)\), \(e_1=P(0\mid1)\), and the rule of Ch. 30 (ex-27) in m-qg is \(m'=(1-e_0-e_1)m+1000(e_1-e_0)\) (readout_affine). With \(e_0=0.02\), \(e_1=0.08\) (illustrative values): \(+1000\to960\) and \(-1000\to-840\) m-qg, that is, amplitude 900 m-qg and shift +60 m-qg (each percentage point of readout error costs 10 m-qg of visibility); correcting amplifies noise by \(1/(1-e_0-e_1)=1.11\times\). It is the standard correction written linearly.

37.7 NV centres: contrast as a budget
With \(n\sim\text{Poisson}(N_b[1-C(1-p_0)])\), the reading of \(p_0\) in m-qg has (nv_sigma_mqg)
\[\sigma_m=\frac{2000\sqrt{1-C(1-p_0)}}{C\sqrt{N_b}}\ \approx\ \frac{2000}{C\sqrt{N_b}}.\]
With \(C=0.3\) and \(N_b=444\,444\): the approximation gives 10.00 m-qg and the exact formula 9.22 m-qg; for exactly 10 m-qg one needs 377 778 photons (nv_photons_for). The contrast \(C=0.3\) costs ≈\(1/C^2=11.1\times\) the photons of \(C=1\). In ODMR (Lorentzian line of 1 MHz, \(C=0.2\), 61 frequencies over \(\pm3\) widths, 1.16 M photons), the Cramér–Rao bound of the center is 8.55 kHz = 305 nT with \(\gamma=28\) GHz/T (odmr_fisher_crb_hz). The line fit does not change with qang; the scale adds the prior count in a unit linear in the population.

text:
qg has no period. \(qg_Z\in[-1,1]\) and the angle \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\). A criterion such as “phase \(=\pi\equiv0.5\) qg cycle” is rewritten as a reading (e.g. \(qg_X=-1\), \(-1000\) m-qg). qga (1 turn = 1000 qga) is periodic, but it is still an angle, not a reading.
A phase does not change \(qg_Z\). A rotation about \(Z\) (Larmor, Aharonov–Bohm, exchange sign) leaves the populations intact: it is read in \(qg_X\) or \(qg_Y\) (Ch. 10, ex-7).
Where there is a probability, there is a reading: reflectance, weight of a state, vacuum occupation.

38.2 Jordan–Wigner: the exchange sign is a reading
With \(a_j^\dagger=\big(\prod_{k<j}Z_k\big)\sigma_j^+\) (jw_creation), the relations \(\{a_i,a_j^\dagger\}=\delta_{ij}\) and \(\{a_i,a_j\}=0\) hold with error 0.0 for 4 modes (anticommutation_error). In a Hadamard test where an auxiliary qubit controls the exchange of occupied modes 0 and 1 (exchange_qgx): with the fermionic exchange (SWAP·CZ) the auxiliary reads \(qg_X=-1000\) m-qg; with a qubit SWAP, \(+1000\) m-qg. The Pauli sign is the difference between the poles of \(qg_X\). The \(Z\) gates of the parity string are exact: the error of a real circuit comes from noise, not from the mapping.

Two non-collinear boosts, \(0.6c\,\hat x\) and \(0.8c\,\hat y\) (boost, wigner_rotation): polar decomposition of \(\Lambda=B_2B_1\) and closed formula agree to \(10^{-14}\): \(\Omega_W=0.3303\) rad \(=18.92^\circ\); a spin that pointed along \(x\) reads \(qg_X=\cos\Omega_W=+945.9\) m-qg; in qga, \(\Omega_W=52.6\) qga. 38.7 Fresnel
Air → glass (\(n=1.5\)) and glass → air (fresnel, tir_phase_difference):

Brewster, \(56.31^\circ\): \(r_p=0\) exactly; \(R_s=0.148\) (−704.1 m-qg). Normal incidence: \(R=0.04\) (−920 m-qg).
Total reflection (critical \(41.81^\circ\)): \(|r_s|=|r_p|=1\) to \(10^{-14}\); the reflectance reads \(+1000\) m-qg and conveys nothing: all the information is in the phases. \(|\delta_p-\delta_s|\) reaches \(45.24^\circ\) at \(51.67^\circ\) and equals \(45^\circ\) at \(50.23^\circ\) and \(53.26^\circ\) (Fresnel rhomb). With linear light at \(45^\circ\) incident at \(45^\circ\): \(qg_Y=\sin|\delta_p-\delta_s|=+600\) m-qg, a Stokes reading (Ch. 9, ex-6).
Goos–Hänchen is not a phase shift but a lateral displacement, from the derivative of the phase (not re-run here).

38.8 Unruh vacuum: the half-angle is the Gudermannian
Each reduced mode is thermal with \(\tanh^2r=e^{-2\pi\omega c/a}\). The vacuum weight is \(p_0=1/\cosh^2r\), and then \(\theta/2=\operatorname{gd}(r)=\arctan(\sinh r)\) to \(2\cdot10^{-16}\) (vacuum_weight, gudermannian). The closed entropy \(S=\cosh^2r\ln\cosh^2r-\sinh^2r\ln\sinh^2r\) agrees with the sum over occupation numbers to \(7\cdot10^{-16}\) up to \(r=1\) and to \(2\cdot10^{-6}\) at \(r=1.5\) (cutoff of 80 levels). An \(SU(1,1)\) transformation is not a rotation: the identity holds for the vacuum weight, not for the transformation.

39.1 The contract
Updated: November 16, 2026
Every adapter receives the same thing: a rotation \(R_Y(\arccos qg_Z)\) and a canonical reading in m-qg (\(1000\,qg_Z\), not qga), with the optional weight filter of Ch. 1–2 (_readings.py). The contract avoids three interface errors: units (pytket measures in half-turns: 500 qga), qubit order (Qiskit puts qubit 0 on the right; Cirq, PennyLane, Braket and pytket, on the left) and physical versus logical position after layout.

text:
qga is not m-qg. The angle is given in qga (1 turn = 1000 qga); the readings, in m-qg (\(1000\,qg_Z\)).
The antiparticle is an inverted reading, not an added angle. \(C\) takes \(\theta\mapsto\pi-\theta\) at the pole-equator of the Dirac qubit and negates \(qg_X,qg_Y,qg_Z\) at once.
What is claimed here is standard. Landau–Zener, Zitterbewegung and charge conjugation are known physics; qang contributes the reading scale and the shot budget.

title: Chapter 40 — Matter and Antimatter Read with qang: Charge Conjugation, Zitterbewegung, Pair Creation and the Invisible Pair
text:
40.2 Charge conjugation: the antipodal map
For \(H=p\sigma_x+m\sigma_z\), \(C\psi=\sigma_y\psi^*\) satisfies \(\sigma_yH^*\sigma_y=-H\), so it takes an energy eigenstate \(+E\) (\(E=\sqrt{p^2+m^2}\)) to one of \(-E\) (conjugate). On the qubit it acts on the three readings as \((qg_X,qg_Y,qg_Z)\mapsto-(qg_X,qg_Y,qg_Z)\): over 500 random eigenstates the error is \(1.1\cdot10^{-13}\) m-qg, and \(qg_Z=+1000\,m/E\) on the positive branch. That map is antiunitary: no gate implements it (the antipode of an unknown state is not obtained with a unitary). Exact consequence: \(|\langle\psi|C\psi\rangle|=0\) for every pure one-qubit state (maximum observed \(6.8\cdot10^{-17}\) over 2000 states), so no pure one-qubit state is its own antiparticle. A Majorana particle needs more space (Ch. 14, ex-11, Majorana phases).

title: Chapter 40 — Matter and Antimatter Read with qang: Charge Conjugation, Zitterbewegung, Pair Creation and the Invisible Pair
text:
40.3 Zitterbewegung as a Rabi problem
A state starting at \(|0\rangle\) (the pole, \(qg_Z=+1000\) m-qg) under \(H\) precesses around \(\hat n=(p,0,m)/E\) with frequency \(2E\):
\[
qg_Z(t)=\frac{m^2}{E^2}+\frac{p^2}{E^2}\cos 2Et=\frac1{\gamma^2}+\beta^2\cos2Et .
\]
With \(p/m=0.75\) (\(\gamma=1.25\), \(\beta=0.6\)) the reading oscillates around \(640.0\) m-qg with amplitude \(360.0\) m-qg; the exact diagonalization (zb_qgz_mqg) agrees with the formula (zb_analytic_mqg) to \(4.5\cdot10^{-13}\) m-qg. It is the same geometry as the area rule of Ch. 2: the detuning is \(m\) and the coupling \(p\).

title: Chapter 40 — Matter and Antimatter Read with qang: Charge Conjugation, Zitterbewegung, Pair Creation and the Invisible Pair
text:
40.4 Pair creation: Landau–Zener
In a uniform field, each mode is an avoided crossing: with \(H=\tfrac{vt}{2}\sigma_z+\tfrac\Delta2\sigma_x\), the probability of staying in the diabatic state is \(e^{-\pi\Delta^2/2v}\) (lz_probability). With \(\Delta=2m\) and \(v=2eE\) it gives the Schwinger rate per mode, \(P=e^{-\pi m^2/eE}\) (pair_probability). Propagating the \(2\times2\) system between \(\pm250\) (lz_numeric), the agreement is \(2.0\cdot10^{-3}\) in the worst case (finite window). The vacuum/pair occupation is read as \(qg=1-2P\) (pair_reading_mqg).

40.5 The singlet pair is invisible in local readings
A particle–antiparticle pair in a spin singlet has \(qg_Z=0\) on each qubit (0.0 and 0.0 m-qg), but \(qg_{ZZ}=-1000\) m-qg (singlet_readings). It is the blindness of the \(Z\) basis of Ch. 34: the local reading does not see the pair; the correlation does.

40.6 How much it costs to see the sign
Distinguishing the \(+1000/\gamma\) branch from the \(-1000/\gamma\) one at \(z\) deviations from zero requires \(N=z^2(\gamma^2-1)\) shots (shots_to_certify_branch). At \(z=3\): 27 shots with \(\gamma=2\) and 443 with \(\gamma=7.089\) (\(\beta=0.99\)). The more relativistic the particle, the closer to the equator the reading sits and the more the branch costs.

section: 41.2 What it adds to the nonlinearity: the information balance
text:
41.2 What it adds to the nonlinearity: the information balance
Let \(U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes I+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes R_y(\alpha)\). Then \(C=\mathrm{Tr}_\mathrm{CTC}U=2\,\mathrm{diag}(1,a)\) with \(a=\cos(\alpha/2)\), and the P-CTC map on the polar angle is
\[
\tan\frac{\theta'}2=a\tan\frac\theta2,\qquad p_\mathrm{post}=\cos^2\frac\theta2+a^2\sin^2\frac\theta2,\qquad \frac{d\theta'}{d\theta}=\frac{a}{p_\mathrm{post}} .
\]
Near the south pole (\(\theta=\pi\)) the amplification is \(1/a\): two nearly equal states end up more separated at the output. But there \(p_\mathrm{post}=a^2\). For \(a=0.5\): amplification 2, \(p_\mathrm{post}=0.25\), ×4 shots per success (pctc_amplification, pctc_p_post).
Exact result. For a family of pure states, the Fisher information per accepted shot is \((d\theta'/d\theta)^2\) and that of the success rate is \((dp/d\theta)^2/[p(1-p)]\). Their sum weighted per input copy is
\[
p\,\Big(\frac{d\theta'}{d\theta}\Big)^2+\frac{(1-a^2)\cos^2(\theta/2)}{p}=\frac{a^2+(1-a^2)\cos^2(\theta/2)}{p}=1 .
\]
With 2000 random pairs \((a,\theta)\), \(|F_\mathrm{total}-1|\le 8.5\cdot10^{-13}\) (pctc_fisher). Postselection does not create information: what the amplified success gains, the failure rate loses. Only at the south pole does the success term equal 1 by itself (\(p\,F_\mathrm{acc}=1.0000\) with \(a=0.5\)); the rest of the circle splits the 1 between the success and the success probability.

title: Chapter 41 — Time Travel Read with qang: the Information Balance of Postselection, the Grandfather Paradox and Fixed Points by Angle
text:
41.3 The grandfather paradox
With \(U=I_\mathrm{CR}\otimes X_\mathrm{CTC}\) (the qubit that returns to the past is flipped): P-CTC gives \(C=\mathrm{Tr}_\mathrm{CTC}U=0\) and \(p_\mathrm{post}=0\): the history never occurs, there is no accepted shot to read. D-CTC solves the fixed point by iterating \(\rho_\mathrm{CTC}\leftarrow\mathrm{Tr}_\mathrm{CR}[U(\rho\otimes\rho_\mathrm{CTC})U^\dagger]\) from \(I/2\): the result is the state with readings \((0,0,0)\) m-qg (the fixed points of \(\rho\mapsto X\rho X\) are all those with \(qg_Y=qg_Z=0\); iteration from \(I/2\) picks the maximum-entropy one), and the chronology-respecting qubit leaves the same as it entered (deutsch_iterate; input \(qg_X=+1000\) m-qg, output \(+1000\) m-qg).

section: 42.2 The light-cone bosonic string: exact counting
text:
42.2 The light-cone bosonic string: exact counting
With \(d=24\) transverse oscillators, the degeneracy of level \(N\) is the coefficient of \(q^N\) in \(\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{-24}\) (colored_partitions): \(1,\,24,\,324,\,3200,\,25650,\,176256\) for \(N=0,\dots,5\). The zero-point energy is \(-(D-2)/24\) (zero_point_energy); the first excited level is massless only if \((D-2)/24=1\), that is \(D=26\) (critical_dimension, unique in \(3\le D<60\)). For the open string, \(\alpha' M^2=N-1\): \(-1\) at \(N=0\) (tachyon) and \(0\) at \(N=1\). In the closed string, level \(N=\tilde N=1\) has \(24\times24=576\) states, which decompose into \(299\) (graviton, symmetric traceless) \(+\,276\) (Kalb–Ramond, antisymmetric) \(+\,1\) (dilaton) (closed_massless_decomposition).
Cost in qubits to label the states of a level (only to size it, the spectrum is not encoded): \(\lceil\log_2 d_N\rceil=5,\,9,\,12,\,15,\,18\) for \(N=1,\dots,5\).

section: 42.3 The level \(N\) as a linear Z reading and its filter under \(T_1\)
text:
42.3 The level \(N\) as a linear Z reading and its filter under \(T_1\)
With one qubit per mode (\(k\)-th mode \(=\) qubit \(k-1\), occupation 0/1: this is the fermionic or “distinct parts” case, not the 24 bosonic oscillators), the level is the weighted weight \(W(x)=\sum_k k\,x_k\). It is linear in the readings: \(\langle N\rangle=\sum_k k\,(1000-m_k)/2000\), with \(m_k\) the \(qg_Z\) reading of qubit \(k-1\) in m-qg (level_from_z, level_from_readings; difference with the histogram \(7\cdot10^{-15}\)). The size of the level-\(N\) sector with \(n=10\) modes is the number of partitions of \(N\) into distinct parts: \(1,1,1,2,2,3,4,5,6,8,10\) (level_sector_size, distinct_partitions).
Budget. With \(n=6\) and uniform \(p\), \(\mathrm{Var}\,N=22.75\); for \(\sigma_N=0.1\) at 95 % one needs \(8740\) Z shots (level_shots), with no additional settings.
Level filter under \(T_1\). Any decay of an occupied mode lowers the level, so the level filter always detects it; the retention is exactly \((1-\gamma)^{|x|}\) (level_filter_damped). For the level-14 state (modes 1, 3, 4, 6): \(\gamma=0.1\) retains \(0.6561=(0.9)^4\); \(\gamma=0.3\) retains \(0.2401\) and the raw mean level is \(9.80\) versus \(14\).
Two complementary blind spots (level_vs_weight_blindness): the exchange \(\{3\}\leftrightarrow\{1,2\}\) conserves the level (3) and changes the weight (\(1\to2\)): the level filter does not see it. The move \(\{1\}\to\{2\}\) conserves the weight and changes the level (\(1\to2\)): the weight filter of Ch. 34 does not see it. Each filter needs to know which quantity the circuit conserves.

text:
42.4 T-duality of the compactified boson
With \(p_{L,R}=n/R\pm wR/\alpha'\) and \((h,\bar h)=(\alpha' p_L^2/4+N-1,\ \alpha' p_R^2/4+\tilde N-1)\), the level matching is \(nw+N-\tilde N=0\) (conformal_weights, closed_spectrum). The spectrum with \(h,\bar h\le2\) and 24 oscillators per side is identical at \(R\) and at \(\alpha'/R\) (exchange \(n\leftrightarrow w\)): checked at \(R=0.5,\,0.7,\,1,\,1.3,\,2,\,3\) (t_dual_equal). Massless states (\(h=\bar h=0\), massless_states): \(R=0.7\) and \(1.3\): \(576\); \(R=0.5\) and \(2\): \(580\); \(R=3\): \(578\); self-dual radius \(R=\sqrt{\alpha'}\): \(676=576+4\cdot24+4\), with \(4\cdot24=96\) vector states at \((n,w)=(\pm1,\pm1)\) (massless_breakdown) and \(4\) scalars at \((\pm2,0),(0,\pm2)\). The enlargement from \(576\) to \(676\) is the extended symmetry of the self-dual radius.

section: 42.5 The radius, read with a single Z basis: an XXZ chain
text:
42.5 The radius, read with a single Z basis: an XXZ chain
The XXZ chain \(H=\sum_i S^x_iS^x_{i+1}+S^y_iS^y_{i+1}+\Delta S^z_iS^z_{i+1}\) is the lattice analogue of a compactified boson; its Luttinger parameter \(K=\pi/(2(\pi-\arccos\Delta))\) (luttinger_k_exact; \(K=1\) at \(\Delta=0\), \(K=1/2\) at \(\Delta=1\)) fixes the radius, with an identification \(K\leftrightarrow R^2/\alpha'\) that depends on convention. In the ring, the variance of the Hamming weight of a block of \(\ell\) qubits, read from a single Z histogram, grows as \((K/\pi^2)\ln[(L/\pi)\sin(\pi\ell/L)]\) (block_weight_variance, luttinger_k_from_variance; fit with even \(\ell\ge4\), because odd \(\ell\) oscillate).

42.6 What it does not measure

It does not measure \(D=26\) as the dimension of spacetime, nor the physical mass spectrum, nor the coupling: they are identities of a model.
The level \(W(x)\) with 0/1 occupation is not the spectrum of the 24 bosonic oscillators; it is the fermionic case. The degeneracies \(d_N\) are counted, not encoded in qubits.
The radius of the XXZ chain is that of a finite-size lattice analogue; the identification with \(R/\sqrt{\alpha'}\) depends on convention.
The local readings \(qg_Z\) and \(qg_S\) still do not measure the central charge (Ch. 33, against); the block variance of §42.5 does depend on \(K\) because it uses the joint histogram of several qubits.

text:
Every result comes with its function in qang.qrobot and its line in tools/verify_cap43.py. Scales: \(m\text{-qg}=1000\,qg_Z\) (reading); the joint angle is given in radians and, when convenient, in qga (1 turn \(=2\pi\) rad \(=1000\) qga; \(\pi/2\) rad \(=250\) qga).
We optimize in \(\theta\) (or in qga), never in \(qg_Z\) without regularization: the flat gradient in \(qg_Z\) diverges at the poles (Ch. 34, THEORY_CORE.md §2.1).
A shot time, a loop rate or an oracle cost is a parameter of the model, not a measurement of this book. Where a number appears, it is what the formula gives for that parameter.
No measured gain status: the chapter compares neither against a real robot nor against a classical controller on data.

title: Chapter 43 — Quantum Robotics and Autonomous Control Read with qang: One Qubit per Joint, the Shot Budget, Real Time and Grover for Trajectory Selection
text:
43.2 Theoretical foundations and mathematical formulation
State space of a joint. A planar arm with \(n\) links, lengths \(\ell_i\) and relative angles \(\theta_i\), has end effector
\[
\mathbf p(\boldsymbol\theta)=\Big(\sum_i \ell_i\cos\phi_i,\ \sum_i \ell_i\sin\phi_i\Big),\qquad \phi_i=\sum_{j\le i}\theta_j,
\]
and Jacobian \(J_{\cdot i}=\partial\mathbf p/\partial\theta_i\). Each joint is encoded in one qubit, \(|\theta\rangle=R_Y(\theta)|0\rangle\), with
\[
p_0=\cos^2\frac\theta2,\qquad qg_Z=\cos\theta,\qquad qg_X=\sin\theta,\qquad m_Z=1000\cos\theta\ \text{m-qg}.
\]
The full circuit is \(U(\boldsymbol\theta)=\bigotimes_i R_Y(\theta_i)\), a product: the decision state is separable and its parameter space is the joint torus \([-\pi,\pi]^n\).
Reading one joint. With \(N\) shots in \(Z\), \(\widehat{qg}_Z=2k_0/N-1\) with \(\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{qg}_Z)=\sin^2\theta/N\). Propagating through \(\hat\theta=\arccos\widehat{qg}_Z\),
\[
\mathrm{Var}(\hat\theta)\simeq\frac{\sin^2\theta/N}{\sin^2\theta}=\frac1N\quad\text{for all }\theta\in(0,\pi),
\qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{qga}}=\frac{1000}{2\pi}\frac1{\sqrt N}=\frac{159.15}{\sqrt N}\ \text{qga}.
\]
This is a constant Fisher information \(I_Z=N\): the angular error does not depend on where the joint is (unlike the error in \(m\)-qg, which vanishes at the poles; Ch. 1).
The sign trap. \(qg_Z=\cos\theta\) is even: \(\theta\) and \(-\theta\) give the same reading, and \(\arccos\) returns \([0,\pi]\) (Ch. 34, arccos_range_trap). A joint with a symmetric range needs a second basis. With \(N\) shots in \(Z\) and \(N\) in \(X\) (\(qg_X=\sin\theta\)),
\[
\hat\theta=\operatorname{atan2}(\widehat{qg}_X,\widehat{qg}_Z),\qquad
\mathrm{Var}(\hat\theta)\simeq\frac{\cos^4\theta+\sin^4\theta}{N}\ \ge\ \frac1{2N}=\mathrm{CRB}(\theta),
\]
with equality only at \(\theta=45^\circ\) (125 qga). The total Fisher information is \(N+N\), and the \(\operatorname{atan2}\) estimator does not saturate it except at \(45^\circ\).
From the axis to the end effector. With independent errors of \(\sigma_\theta=1/\sqrt N\) per joint, the mean-square error of the end effector to first order is
\[
\mathrm{RMS}(\mathbf p)=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{tr}(JJ^{\mathsf T})}{N}},\qquad
N(\varepsilon)=\Big\lceil \frac{z^2\,\mathrm{tr}(JJ^{\mathsf T})}{\varepsilon^2}\Big\rceil .
\]
This is the shot budget before executing the action: it depends on the posture (through \(J\)), not on the unit.
Real-time budget. With loop rate \(f\), time per shot \(t_s\) and overhead \(t_0\), the shots per cycle are \(N_c=\lfloor(1/f-t_0)/t_s\rfloor\) and \(\sigma_\theta=1/\sqrt{N_c}\). The loop meets the tolerance only if \(N_c\ge N(\varepsilon)\), that is, if \(f\le 1/(t_0+N(\varepsilon)\,t_s)\).
A drifting joint. If \(\theta_{t+1}=\theta_t+w\) (\(\mathrm{Var}\,w=q\)) and each cycle delivers \(\hat\theta_t\) with variance \(r=1/N\), the scalar Kalman filter (Kalman 1960) has steady-state prior variance \(P^-=\tfrac12\big(q+\sqrt{q^2+4qr}\big)\) and posterior variance \(P=P^--q\). What qang contributes is the value of \(r\) (\(1/N\), or \((159.15)^2/N\) qga²); the filter is classical.
Trajectory selection with Grover. With \(N_c\) candidates of which \(M\) are collision-free (\(\sin^2\theta_0=M/N_c\)), \(k\) iterations give success \(\sin^2\big((2k+1)\theta_0\big)\) (Ch. 3), with \(k^\star=\lfloor\pi/(4\theta_0)\rfloor\). Unstructured classical search needs \((N_c+1)/(M+1)\) expected evaluations, and \(\Omega(\sqrt{N_c/M})\) queries is a quantum lower bound in the oracle model (Bennett et al. 1997; Grover 1996). The classical/quantum ratio grows as \((2/\pi)\sqrt{N_c}\) for \(M=1\).
Variational optimization. A parametric circuit (Kandala et al. 2017; Cerezo et al. 2021) in inverse kinematics minimizes \(C(\boldsymbol\theta)=\lVert\mathbf p(\boldsymbol\theta)-\mathbf p^\star\rVert^2\); the gradient of each reading comes from the parameter-shift rule, \(\partial qg_Z/\partial\theta=[qg_Z(\theta+\pi/2)-qg_Z(\theta-\pi/2)]/2=-\sin\theta\), with a shift of 250 qga. Since \(C\) is an exact classical function of \(\boldsymbol\theta\), the circuit only adds shot noise: that use stays unverified (§43.7).

The flow is classical–quantum–classical: the quantum part happens only in the middle box, and what qang adds is the pre-check (how many shots, how much error, whether it fits the cycle) and the reading with its uncertainty in qga. Kinematics and the filter are classical and are not replaced.

43.4 Practical implementation (qang + Qiskit)
import numpy as np
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler          # exact Qiskit 2.x simulator
from qang.qrobot import (two_link_ik, planar_fk, preflight, joint_from_readings, joint_sigma_qga)

LINKS, TARGET = (1.0, 0.8), (1.2, 0.9)
theta_ref = two_link_ik(TARGET, *LINKS)                   # (0.1279, 1.1796) rad: classical reference

# 1. Pre-check, before touching the environment (illustrative parameters: 1 ms per shot)
fast = preflight(theta_ref, LINKS, eps=0.02, rate_hz=100, t_shot_s=1e-3)
slow = preflight(theta_ref, LINKS, eps=0.02, rate_hz=0.1, t_shot_s=1e-3)
print(fast["shots_required"], fast["shots_available"], fast["feasible"])   # 7225.0 10.0 0.0
print(slow["feasible"], round(slow["sigma_theta_qga"], 2))                  # 1.0 1.59

# 2. Reading per joint: R_Y(θ)|0>, two bases to recover the sign
sampler = StatevectorSampler(seed=43)

def read_joint(theta, n):
    qg = []
    for basis in ("Z", "X"):
        qc = QuantumCircuit(1, 1)
        qc.ry(theta, 0)
        if basis == "X":
            qc.h(0)                                       # measure X: H before measuring
        qc.measure(0, 0)
        counts = sampler.run([qc], shots=n).result()[0].data.c.get_counts()
        qg.append(2 * counts.get("0", 0) / n - 1)
    return joint_from_readings(*qg)                       # atan2(qg_X, qg_Z)

n = int(slow["shots_required"])
theta_hat = [read_joint(t, n) for t in theta_ref]
err = np.linalg.norm(planar_fk(theta_hat, LINKS) - planar_fk(theta_ref, LINKS))
print(round(err, 3), "versus tolerance 0.02")              # a single run: of the order of 0.02 or less
Interpretation.

The pre-check is deterministic and reproducible: for the target \((1.2,\,0.9)\) and \(\varepsilon=0.02\), 7225 shots per joint are needed. At 100 Hz and 1 ms per shot, 10 fit, \(\sigma_\theta=0.316\) rad (\(18.1^\circ\), \(50.3\) qga) and the end-effector error would be \(0.54\). At \(0.1\) Hz, 10 000 shots fit, \(\sigma_\theta=0.01\) rad (\(1.59\) qga) and the loop is feasible.
The two-basis reading costs \(2N\) shots per joint; its expected error is \(\le\varepsilon\) (at \(45^\circ\) it is half the variance of the \(Z\)-only case). A single run fluctuates around that RMS: it is not a per-run guarantee.
The print values of step 2 are not a measurement of this book. Qiskit was not installed in the environment where the chapter was written; the identities behind it (variances, RMS and budget) are verified with NumPy binomial shots in tools/verify_cap43.py. Whoever reproduces the block should check the Qiskit output in their own environment.

Tracking a drifting joint (verified in tools/verify_cap43.py, §[5]): with \(q=4\cdot10^{-4}\) rad² per cycle and \(N=400\) shots, the steady-state posterior variance is \(8.20\cdot10^{-4}\) rad² (simulated: \(8.21\cdot10^{-4}\)), that is, \(\sigma=0.029\) rad versus \(0.050\) rad without the filter.

Limitations. (i) Real time: with millisecond shot times, a tolerance of \(0.01\) rad on one joint limits the loop to \(0.1\) Hz; with the queue time of a cloud service, worse. A kHz control loop cannot be closed today with quantum readings by shots. (ii) NISQ: the model is one noiseless qubit per joint; with readout noise the affine readout must be calibrated (qang.qchar, Ch. 30); the gate noise of an \(R_Y\) is small, but the readout noise is not. (iii) Grover: the saving is in queries, and it requires a coherent collision oracle whose cost does not enter \((2/\pi)\sqrt N\); Chapter 3 measures that with noise, reading \(qg_Z\) per qubit loses against the string histogram (66 % versus 91 % at \(n=5\)). (iv) Variational: the kinematics is an exact classical function; a parametric circuit does not improve it (§43.7).
Future directions, without result. Quantum SLAM: qang has no verified formulation; it would be a hypothesis for a pre-registered experiment (data association as a search in a weight sector would be a hypothesis), unverified. Optimal control under uncertainty: the possible contribution is the \(r=1/N\) of the measurement inside a classical LQG; no advantage is claimed. Arms with more degrees of freedom: \(N(\varepsilon)\) grows with \(\mathrm{tr}(JJ^{\mathsf T})\), that is, with the reach of the arm.

Rewards, steps and the exploration floor are parameters of the model, not measurements. Where a number appears, it comes from the formula with that parameter.

title: Chapter 44 — Quantum Agentic AI Read with qang: Born Policies, the Angle as Natural Gradient, the Decision Reading and Shot Allocation Across Tools
text:
44.2 Theoretical foundations and mathematical formulation
The minimal agent. A two-action agent prepares \(R_Y(\theta)|0\rangle\) and measures in \(Z\); the action is the outcome. Then
\[
\pi(0|\theta)=\cos^2\frac\theta2=p_0,\qquad \pi(1|\theta)=\sin^2\frac\theta2,\qquad qg_Z=\cos\theta=\pi(0)-\pi(1),
\]
and the decision state is the point on the Bloch sphere; the policy is a meridian. With mean rewards \(r_0,r_1\) and \(\Delta=r_0-r_1\), the expected return is \(J(\theta)=r_0\pi(0)+r_1\pi(1)\) and
\[
\partial_\theta J=-\frac{\Delta\sin\theta}{2},\qquad
\partial_\theta\log\pi(0)=-\tan\frac\theta2,\qquad \partial_\theta\log\pi(1)=\cot\frac\theta2 .
\]
Fisher information. \(I(\theta)=\pi(0)\tan^2\tfrac\theta2+\pi(1)\cot^2\tfrac\theta2=\sin^2\tfrac\theta2+\cos^2\tfrac\theta2=1\) for every \(\theta\): it is the Fubini–Study metric on the meridian (Ch. 9). In \(qg_Z\) the same information is \(1/(1-qg_Z^2)\), which diverges at the poles; that is why the flat gradient in \(qg_Z\) is useless and the natural one in \(qg_Z\) coincides with the Euclidean one in \(\theta\) (Ch. 34).
The gradient flow. With the exact gradient, \(\dot\theta=\eta\,\partial_\theta J=-\tfrac{\eta\Delta}{2}\sin\theta\), which integrates in closed form:
\[
\tan\frac{\theta_t}{2}=\tan\frac{\theta_0}{2}\,e^{-\eta\Delta t/2}.
\]
With the logit \(\phi=\ln\frac{\pi(0)}{\pi(1)}=2\ln\cot\frac\theta2\) this is \(\phi_t=\phi_0+\eta\Delta t\): plain gradient descent in \(\theta\) is the natural gradient in the logit, because the Fisher information of the logit is \(\pi_0\pi_1\) and \(F^{-1}\partial_\phi J=\Delta\). The time for the worse action to fall to \(\pi_\ast\) is
\[
T_\theta=\frac{\ln\frac{1-\pi_\ast}{\pi_\ast}-\phi_0}{\eta\Delta},\qquad
T_{\text{flat logit}}=\frac{F(\phi_\ast)-F(\phi_0)}{\eta\Delta},\quad F(\phi)=2\sinh\phi+2\phi,
\]
and \(T_\theta\propto\ln(1/\pi_\ast)\) versus \(T_{\text{flat logit}}\propto1/\pi_\ast\). The difference is not an intrinsic quantum advantage: it is the choice of the metric (of a preconditioner). The natural gradient in the logit gives the same curve as the plain one in \(\theta\).
The pole. The REINFORCE estimator (Williams 1992) \(g=r_a\,\partial_\theta\log\pi(a)\) is unbiased, with
\[
\mathbb E[g]=-\frac{\Delta\sin\theta}{2},\qquad
\mathbb E[g^2]=r_0^2\sin^2\tfrac\theta2+r_1^2\cos^2\tfrac\theta2 ,
\]
so near a pole the mean vanishes as \(\sin\theta\) and the variance stays at \(r_1^2\) (or \(r_0^2\)): the episodes needed to resolve the sign, \(z^2\mathrm{Var}(g)/\mathbb E[g]^2\), diverge as \(1/\sin^2\theta\). And at \(\theta=0\) or \(\pi\) the gradient is exactly zero: an agent that reaches a bad pole does not leave it. The way out is an exploration floor: \(\theta\in[\theta_{\min},\pi-\theta_{\min}]\) with \(\theta_{\min}=2\arcsin\sqrt{p_{\min}}\) guarantees \(\pi(a)\ge p_{\min}\).
The decision reading. Before acting, the qang measures say how decided the policy is: \(qg_Z\) and its reading \(m_Z\) in m-qg, the entropy \(qg_S=H(p_0)\) in bits, \(qg_{SNR}=|\cot\theta|\) and the shots for the sign of \(qg_Z\) to be \(z\) deviations away, \((z/qg_{SNR})^2\) (Ch. 1). At the equator \(qg_S=1\) bit and the sign cannot be decided with any number of shots.
Tool orchestration: shot allocation. If an agent queries \(K\) readings \(qg_{Z,i}\) (one per tool or subroutine) with a budget \(B\), the sum of variances is \(\sum_i\sin^2\theta_i/n_i\), and with \(\sum n_i=B\) the minimum is \(n_i\propto\sin\theta_i\):
\[
\frac{V_{\text{uniform}}}{V_{\text{optimal}}}=\frac{K\sum_i\sin^2\theta_i}{\big(\sum_i\sin\theta_i\big)^2}\ \ge1\quad\text{(Cauchy–Schwarz)},
\]
with equality only if all the \(\sin\theta_i\) coincide. What qang contributes is that \(\sin\theta_i=\sqrt{1-qg_{Z,i}^2}\) is known from a pilot reading.
What is not there. A one-qubit policy has the same distribution as a classical coin of bias \(p_0\): quantum hardware changes neither the policy nor its learning. The learning advantages documented for quantum policies (Jerbi et al. 2021; Dunjko et al. 2016; Skolik et al. 2022) refer to models with several qubits and entanglement, or to quantum access to the environment, and this chapter neither reproduces nor claims them.

44.3 Hybrid architecture and integration with qang v0.16
 environment ──obs──► [PERCEPTION: state qubit(s) → qg_Z, qg_X]            (Qiskit)
                         │ readings with intervals (qang.probability, qang.statistics)
                         ▼
              [classical REASONING]  ◄── qang.qagent: decision_report, time_to_wrong_probability,
                         │                 episodes_for_gradient_sign, neyman_allocation
                         │ plan: shots per tool, step η, floor p_min
                         ▼
              [tool ORCHESTRATOR]  (deterministic planner; an LLM can take this place [@yao2023react])
                         │ calls: simulator/QPU · Grover (Ch. 43) · qg_Z estimator
                         ▼
              [ACTION: one shot of the policy qubit] ──► environment ──reward R──┐
                         ▲                                                       │
                         └──────── REINFORCE update in θ (with floor) ◄──────────┘
The quantum part happens in two boxes, perception (optional) and action; reasoning, the orchestrator and the update are classical. What qang adds to the reasoning is a pre-check: how much the policy trusts its action, how many steps the flow predicts, how many episodes the gradient sign costs and how to split the shots.

44.4 Practical implementation (qang + Qiskit)
import numpy as np
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler          # exact Qiskit 2.x simulator
from qang.qagent import (decision_report, exploration_floor, score, time_to_wrong_probability,
                         neyman_allocation, uniform_to_neyman_ratio)

MEANS, ETA, P_FLOOR, STEPS = (0.7, 0.3), 0.05, 0.01, 400    # Bernoulli environment and agent parameters
LO = exploration_floor(P_FLOOR)                              # θ_min = 0.2003 rad
sampler = StatevectorSampler(seed=44)
rng = np.random.default_rng(44)

# 1. Prior REASONING: what the flow predicts and how decided the policy is
print(round(time_to_wrong_probability(np.pi / 2, ETA, MEANS[0] - MEANS[1], 0.05), 1))   # 147.2 steps for π(worse) ≤ 5 %
d = decision_report(0.4)
print(round(d["qg_Z"], 3), round(d["m_Z"]), round(d["qg_S"], 3), d["shots_for_sign"])    # 0.921 921 0.24 2.0

# 2. ACTION: one shot of the policy qubit
def act(theta):
    qc = QuantumCircuit(1, 1)
    qc.ry(theta, 0)
    qc.measure(0, 0)
    counts = sampler.run([qc], shots=1).result()[0].data.c.get_counts()
    return int(next(iter(counts)))                           # 0 or 1

# 3. Perception-reasoning-action loop: REINFORCE in θ with an exploration floor
theta = np.pi / 2
for _ in range(STEPS):
    a = act(theta)
    r = float(rng.random() < MEANS[a])                       # Bernoulli reward from the environment
    theta = float(np.clip(theta + ETA * r * score(a, theta), LO, np.pi - LO))
print(round(float(np.sin(theta / 2) ** 2), 3))               # π(worse action): of the order of 0.01–0.02 (floor 0.01)

# 4. Orchestration: split B shots among K=4 pilot readings
thetas = [0.2, 1.0, np.pi / 2, 2.9]
print(np.round(neyman_allocation(thetas, 4000)).astype(int).tolist(), round(uniform_to_neyman_ratio(thetas), 3))
# [349, 1477, 1755, 420] 1.389
Interpretation.

The values of steps 1 and 4 are deterministic and reproducible. The flow predicts 147.2 steps to bring the worse action down to \(5\%\) with \(\eta=0.05\) and \(\Delta=0.4\); the policy at \(\theta=0.4\) reads \(qg_Z=0.921\) (921 m-qg), \(qg_S=0.240\) bits and needs 2 shots to fix the sign at \(3\sigma\). The optimal allocation for \(\theta=(0.2,\,1.0,\,\pi/2,\,2.9)\) gives \((349,\,1477,\,1755,\,420)\) and lowers the sum of variances by \(1.389\) with respect to the uniform split.
Step 3 is stochastic. With the same loop in NumPy (tools/verify_cap44.py uses run_bandit, which draws the action with the same probability \(\cos^2(\theta/2)\)), 300 runs of 400 steps give a mean \(\pi(\text{worse})\) of \(0.020\) and a median of \(0.010\) (the floor). A single run with Qiskit varies; the printed value is an order of magnitude, not a guarantee.
Qiskit was not installed in the environment where the chapter was written: the block was not executed, and its step-3 output remains to be checked in the reader’s environment. The identities behind it are verified with NumPy sampling.
Agreement with the flow (verified): with \(\eta=0.02\) and 100 steps, 400 Bernoulli runs give \(\pi(\text{worse})=0.316\) against \(0.310\) predicted by the closed flow.

Limitations. (i) Latency: an action is one shot, and the time per shot plus the queue of a cloud service make an interactive loop of hundreds of steps on a QPU unviable; on a simulator there is no problem, but there is no advantage either. (ii) Classical equivalence: a one-qubit policy is a biased coin; the benefit of the \(\theta\) parametrization is a choice of metric that a classical natural gradient reproduces. (iii) Several qubits: the advantages in the literature require entanglement or quantum access to the environment; qang has no verified result there, and THEORY_CORE.md (§2) recalls that reading \(qg_Z\) per qubit loses against the string histogram (Ch. 3). (iv) Noise: the model is ideal; with readout noise the affine readout must be calibrated (Ch. 30) before using \(qg_Z\) as a policy.
Future directions, without result. Orchestration by a language model: a ReAct-type agent (Yao et al. 2023) could call the functions of qang.qagent as tools; there is no experiment in this book, unverified. Multi-qubit policies and quantum Q-learning (Skolik et al. 2022): the qang metric for several qubits (Ch. 5, local radius) is a starting point, unverified. Natural gradient with a floor: test with a pre-registered experiment whether the optimal exploration floor \(p_{\min}\) depends on \(\Delta\).

title: Appendix A — Catalogue of the 15 fundamental gates in qg representation
text:
A.1 Fixed single-qubit gates
This appendix collects the action of the gates of qang.formulation on the qg readings. A gate \(U\) transforms each Pauli reading by conjugation,
\[
qg'_P = qg_{U^\dagger P U},
\]
so it is enough to say what each local reading becomes. The tables are not written by hand: tools/make_appendices.py generates them from formulation.gate_table, is_clifford, conserves_weight and gate_radius_class. If the code changes, they are regenerated. In Pauli strings the leftmost letter is qubit 0, which is the control of CX and CZ, both controls of Toffoli and the control of Fredkin.
Why fifteen. The module defines 16 matrices: six fixed single-qubit gates, four parametric ones and six multi-qubit gates. \(R_Z(\varphi)\) and the phase gate \(P(\varphi)\) differ only by a global phase, \(P(\varphi)=e^{i\varphi/2}R_Z(\varphi)\), so they act identically on every reading and count as one in qg.
Clifford gates permute the readings with signs, and \(T\) mixes them. The diagonal gates (\(Z\), \(S\), \(T\)) leave \(qg_Z\) alone: they do not move populations, only the phase, which is read in \(qg_X\) and \(qg_Y\). Conserving the weight is what allows the filter of Chapters 21 and 22.

From \(|0\rangle\), \(R_X(\theta)\) and \(R_Y(\theta)\) are the Chapter 1 probability equation: the gate angle is the qang angle and the reading is \(m=1000\cos\theta\). \(R_Z\) and \(P\) do not change the \(Z\) reading. No rotation about \(X\) or \(Y\) conserves the weight: it moves population between \(|0\rangle\) and \(|1\rangle\). That is why the layers used with the filter are made of Givens (RBS) rotations between pairs, not of single-qubit rotations.
On the angular qga scale of Chapter 1 (Section 1.4), with 1000 qga per turn, a gate angle is written without factors of \(\pi\): \(\theta=2\pi\,\theta_{qga}/1000\) and, from \(|0\rangle\), \(m=1000\cos(2\pi\,\theta_{qga}/1000)\). So \(R_X(500\ \text{qga})\) is \(X\) up to a global phase and reads \(-1000\) m-qg, \(R_Y(250\ \text{qga})\) leaves the qubit on the equator (\(m=0\)) and \(R_Z(\varphi)\) turns the phase by \(\varphi_{qga}\) thousandths of a turn. The script checks the first two.

Radius. “Preserves”: every local radius stays 1 for pure product inputs. “Permutes”: the radii are exchanged (SWAP). “Entangles”: some product input ends with deficit \(1-r_q^2>0\). The maximal deficit, 1, takes a qubit to the centre of the sphere (Chapter 5).

A.4 Update for the rewrite (Chapters 7–44)
The “chapter N” references in this appendix use the numbering of cap01.qmd–cap36.qmd. The rewrite (Parts III–XIV, qjax07–qjax44) uses the new numbering: 1–6 unchanged; 7–29 shift by +3 (7–9 are new); 30–35 shift by +4; 33 and 42 are string theory; 43 and 44 are robotics and agentic AI.
Weight-conserving gates: CZ, Fredkin, SWAP, iSWAP (formulation.conserves_weight). The other multi-qubit gates (CX, Toffoli) change the weight.
Reading limit (Ch. 34, formerly 30; qang.qlimits). Entangling cannot be seen in \(qg_Z\): the 4-qubit ring graph state, built with CZ, has \(qg_Z=0.0\) on every qubit (0.0 m-qg) and four \(XZZ\) stabilizers equal to \(1\). With the \(Z\) reading alone it cannot be told from \(|+\rangle^{\otimes4}\).
Qubit order across SDKs (Ch. 36, formerly 32; qang.qarch.convention_error_mqg): the table above puts qubit 0 on the left, like Cirq and PennyLane; Qiskit puts it on the right.

title: Appendix B — Transition formulas, Gell-Mann matrices and Chebyshev polynomials
text:
B.1 Single-qubit formulas
This appendix gathers in one place the closed forms used in Chapters 2 and 3: the universal gate and the reflections written in \(q=qg_Z\), the transition probability, the generalization of \(qg_Z\) to qudits with the diagonal Gell-Mann matrices, and the Grover trajectory as a Chebyshev polynomial (notes, §37 and §166). There are no new results. What it adds is the check: tools/make_appendices.py evaluates each formula of qang.algebra against direct linear algebra on 2000 random states and writes the maximal error here. If a formula were wrong, the script would stop.
With \(q=qg_Z=\cos\theta\), \(\cos\tfrac\theta2=\sqrt{(1+q)/2}\) and \(\sin\tfrac\theta2=\sqrt{(1-q)/2}\). The pure state with polar bias \(q\) and azimuth \(\varphi\) is
\[
|\psi(q,\varphi)\rangle=\sqrt{\tfrac{1+q}{2}}\,|0\rangle+e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{\tfrac{1-q}{2}}\,|1\rangle,\qquad \vec r=\big(\sqrt{1-q^2}\cos\varphi,\ \sqrt{1-q^2}\sin\varphi,\ q\big).
\]
On the angular qga scale of Chapter 1 (Section 1.4), with \(\theta=2\pi\,\theta_{qga}/1000\), the bias is \(q=\cos(2\pi\,\theta_{qga}/1000)\) and the amplitudes are \(\cos(\pi\,\theta_{qga}/1000)\) and \(\sin(\pi\,\theta_{qga}/1000)\): the formulas below do not change, only the unit of the angle.
The formulas are:
\[
U_3^{qg}(q,\varphi,\lambda)=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt{\tfrac{1+q}{2}} & -e^{i\lambda}\sqrt{\tfrac{1-q}{2}}\\ e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{\tfrac{1-q}{2}} & e^{i(\varphi+\lambda)}\sqrt{\tfrac{1+q}{2}}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \big|U_{ij}\big|^2=\begin{pmatrix}\tfrac{1+q}{2} & \tfrac{1-q}{2}\\ \tfrac{1-q}{2} & \tfrac{1+q}{2}\end{pmatrix}
\tag{B.1}\]
\[
I-2|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=-q\,Z-\sqrt{1-q^2}\,X,\qquad 2|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|-I=q\,Z+\sqrt{1-q^2}\,X
\tag{B.2}\]
\[
|\langle\psi_1|\psi_2\rangle|^2=\frac{1+\vec r_1\cdot\vec r_2}{2}\ \xrightarrow{\ \varphi_1=\varphi_2\ }\ \frac{1+q_1q_2+\sqrt{(1-q_1^2)(1-q_2^2)}}{2}
\tag{B.3}\]
The transition matrix is doubly stochastic, rational in \(q\) and independent of the phases: the probability a gate leaves is read without trigonometry. With \((q,\varphi,\lambda)=(1,0,0)\), \((-1,0,\pi)\), \((1,0,\pi)\) and \((0,0,\pi)\), Equation B.1 gives exactly \(I\), \(X\), \(Z\) and \(H\); the script checks it. The reflector and the diffuser are the same operator with opposite sign, and both are linear combinations of \(Z\) and \(X\) with coefficients \(q\) and \(\sqrt{1-q^2}\) (Chapter 3).

title: Appendix B — Transition formulas, Gell-Mann matrices and Chebyshev polynomials
text:
B.2 Diagonal Gell-Mann matrices
A \(d\)-level qudit has \(d^2-1\) generators of \(\mathfrak{su}(d)\), the generalized Gell-Mann matrices. Only \(d-1\) of them are diagonal: they form the Cartan subalgebra and are the only ones read by measuring in the computational basis. They are
\[
\lambda_k=\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{k(k+1)}}\;\mathrm{diag}(\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{k},-k,0,\dots,0),\qquad k=1,\dots,d-1,\qquad \mathrm{Tr}(\lambda_j\lambda_k)=2\delta_{jk},
\tag{B.4}\]
and their expectation values are linear in the populations \(p\) and determine them:
\[
\langle\lambda_k\rangle=\sum_i p_i\,(\lambda_k)_{ii},\qquad p=\frac1d+\frac12\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}\langle\lambda_k\rangle\,\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_k).
\tag{B.5}\]

title: Appendix B — Transition formulas, Gell-Mann matrices and Chebyshev polynomials
section: B.3 Chebyshev polynomials and the Grover trajectory
text:
B.3 Chebyshev polynomials and the Grover trajectory
With amplitude \(a=\sin^2t\) and the good/bad flag read as a qubit, \(qg_0=1-2a=\cos2t\). Each Grover iteration adds \(2t\) to the angle, so after \(k\) iterations
\[
qg_k=T_{2k+1}(qg_0),\qquad T_m(\cos x)=\cos mx,
\tag{B.6}\]
with \(T_m\) the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind. Since \(T_m'=m\,U_{m-1}\) and \(1-T_m^2=(1-q^2)\,U_{m-1}^2\), the one-shot Fisher information at depth \(m\) is
\[
F_m(qg_0)=\frac{m^2}{1-qg_0^2},
\tag{B.7}\]
the factor \(m^2\) over the depth-1 information, the same along the whole fringe. It is the qg form of the known \(4m^2\) for the angle (Suzuki et al. 2020).

title: Appendix C — The echo-calibration protocol and inversion in Hamming sectors (§105–§108)
text:
C.1 The protocol
Chapter 22 explains why the echo is needed: the qg filter discards the shots that left the sector, but it does not see the errors that move an excitation from one qubit to another without changing the weight. This appendix gives the protocol step by step, what it costs, an exact example generated by tools/make_appendices.py with the functions of qang.sectors, and the record of the four pre-registered runs of the notes.
crumbs: Appendices
C  The echo-calibration protocol and inversion in Hamming sectors (§105–§108)

title: Appendix C — The echo-calibration protocol and inversion in Hamming sectors (§105–§108)
text:
Sector. \(n\) qubits and weight \(w\): the sector has \(D=\binom{n}{w}\) basis states, \(|e_1\rangle,\dots,|e_D\rangle\) (sector_states).
Echoes. For each \(j\): prepare \(|e_j\rangle\) with \(X\) gates, apply the network \(W\) and then \(W^\dagger\), and measure in \(Z\). Without errors the circuit returns to \(|e_j\rangle\). The notes use 4000 shots per echo.
Matrix. Filter each echo to the sector (filter_distribution). Its distribution over the \(D\) states is column \(j\) of \(M\), with \(M_{ij}=P(e_i\text{ measured}\mid e_j\text{ prepared})\) (echo_transfer_matrix).
Root. The circuit to be read has half the gates of the echo, so it is corrected with \(A=M^{1/2}\): the principal, real, non-negative, column-normalized root (matrix_power_stochastic).
Unmixing. Filter the circuit’s distribution, \(f\), and solve \(Ax=f\) with \(x\ge0\) by non-negative least squares; normalize \(x\) (unmix_sector).
Reading. Each qubit reads \(m_Z(q)=1000\,(1-2p_q)\) with the populations of \(x\).
Before using it. Simulate without noise at the same shots to know the sampling error. The echo helps when the filtered error is well above that level, and not when it is already almost all shot noise (§108).

title: Appendix C — The echo-calibration protocol and inversion in Hamming sectors (§105–§108)
text:
C.3 An exact example
The script builds an in-sector channel \(K\) on 5 qubits and weight 1, with probability 0.90 of staying on the right qubit, and a T1 loss of 15% of the shots to \(|00000\rangle\), which reads \(+1000\) m-qg on every qubit. The echo applies \(K\) twice, so \(M=K^2\) (mean diagonal 0.81), and the principal root recovers \(K\) exactly. That is the assumption behind \(M^{1/2}\): that the way back has the same error as the way out. In §105 the full \(M\) did better on Forte-1, so it does not always hold.



Table C.2: No shot noise. The filter removes the loss; \(M^{1/2}\) undoes \(K\); the full \(M\) over-corrects and ends near the filter alone.





readout

Why non-negative least squares and not the inverse. With 1000 shots per run, in 37 of 300 runs the direct inverse \(A^{-1}f\) gives some negative population, which is not a probability. The non-negative solution never does. The mean \(qg_Z\) error is almost the same: 21.6 m-qg with the inverse and 21.5 m-qg with the non-negative solution. What is gained is that the result is always a distribution, not accuracy; that is why the usual readout mitigation also restricts the solution to the simplex.

E.1 Falsification statement
The book’s plan announced a full count of §1–§164 here. Chapter 28 explains why it was not done: the sections before §71 hardly use pre-registration, and many later ones leave their verdicts only in prose, worded differently. This appendix lists what can be checked with code. tools/make_appendices.py generates it with the same functions as the Chapter 28 figure (tools/make_cap28_figures.py), so its totals are the chapter’s.

title: Appendix E — Falsification register: the predictions the repository allows one to check
text:
Definitions and identities are not falsified by experiments. The qg unit, the milli-qang, the probability equation and the formulas of Appendices A and B are proven or checked to machine precision in tests/. If one fails, it is a code bug, not a result.
Empirical claims are. Each says that a reading with qang is more accurate, cheaper or more stable than without qang, and it is fixed with a threshold before running. A failed prediction is published with its number and not rewritten.
What would falsify the programme as a whole. That the advantages of Chapter 29 did not repeat on real hardware with thresholds fixed in advance. Today there are three runs on IQM Garnet, with 12 of 13 predictions passed, but only one tests an advantage: §165, the weight filter on neutrinos. §168 and §170 test the scale and the reading, not an advantage. That is too little to decide.
